title: State Bicycle Co 6061 Trail+ Fat Bike V2
content:
New for the 26/27 winter riding season, State Bicycle Co brings back a classic: its 6061 Trail+ Fat Bike, now updated to V2…

State’s Fat Bike hasn’t received a substantial update in a decade. The new model joins the State Trail Family as the Trail+ Fat Bike v2, featuring an all-new hydroformed 6061 aluminum frame, modern geometry, and specs ready for winter and desert riding.

Highlights include the 66º head tube angle, UDH compatibility, Carbon Fork Upgrade, mounts galore, and Tektro hydraulic brakes with 180 rotors. The Shimano drivetrain offers a whopping 409% range in a durable, price-conscious package. Fat bikes are ridden where cadence collapses: soft sand, deep snow, loaded climbs. Range matters, gear count doesn’t. Complete bikes start at just over 1K, keeping with State’s ethos of accessible bikes for all riders.

This is a completely new frame, with a much slacker front end and hydraulic brakes. The 6061 Trail+ v2 trades its predecessor’s conservative numbers for a 66° head angle, 455 mm chainstays, and a 50mm stem on a 740 mm bar — modern trail geometry applied to a fat bike. It rolls on Kenda Juggernaut 26 x 4.5″ tires, with room for 4.8″

Specs:

  • $1,199.99
  • 26 x 4.8″ clearance
  • Geometry — all sizes
  • Head tube angle: 66°
  • Seat tube angle: 74°
  • Chainstay / rear center: 455mm
  • Bottom bracket drop: 65mm
  • Fork offset: 45mm
  • Fork axle-to-crown: 485mm
  • Trail: ~109mm
